summary: P1/P2 disprove the total-homology naturality and unrestricted coefficient assertions. P3's finite filtered-extension example refutes A.2, whose uniqueness principle is explicitly invoked on p43 for the completed Kauffman-state result used in Section5. P1-P3 are Major, P4-P9 Minor within stated limits. Neither the completed Theorem5.11 conclusion nor DGR inequality is disproved.

problems.title: Total Koszul homology fails the asserted natural state-space identification

source_claim.claim: The total H(dHH+d0) functor is naturally isomorphic to S0 by the identity on the ordinary closed-web Soergel quotient.

assumptions: Coefficient field Q of characteristic zero
Elementary pointed annular one-dumbbell web D2
Outer output y1=0; permitted formal grading shifts for dotted cylinder

counterexample.proof: 1-x1 coprime to x1*x2, hence nonzerodivisor. Cokernel Q with x1=y2=1,x2=0. Dot y2 acts1. Direct two-color pairing gives S1=Q[a,b]/(a+b,ab), S0=Qa, both dots0. Naturality for shifted dotted cylinder equates an invertible map with0. Closed HH0 also requires x2=y2, impossible in this cokernel.
counterexample.correct_result: Equal vector-space dimension does not give a natural isomorphism; iterated H(HH,d0) has x2=y2=0 instead.

counterevidence: The source's numerical dimension1 is correct.
Associated graded may restore dot action; separately cited RW22 spectral sequence is not disproved.
problems.impact: False core functor identification used in the supplied first spectral-sequence argument; not a disproof of every possible DGR proof.

correction.statement: Replace unfiltered total homology by a precisely specified filtered/associated-graded or iterated construction and prove naturality and target. Regrading alone cannot fix identity versus zero.
correction.verification_status: Supported within the explicitly stated boundary; see current English report and analytic notes

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: For the admissible pointed index-two dumbbell over Q, the reduced algebra is B=Q[x1,x2]/(x1*x2), and the total Koszul differential is multiplication by 1-x1. It is injective since 1-x1 is coprime to x1*x2 in the ambient polynomial ring. The cokernel is Q with x1=y2=1 and x2=0, so the y2 dot acts as identity. On the graded one-dimensional S0 state space the corresponding positive-degree dot is zero. Viewing the dotted cylinder as a morphism to a formal grading shift respects the degree-zero morphism convention, so naturality cannot intertwine these actions.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Both numerical dimensions are one, which does not establish naturality. Iterated rather than total homology has the zero dot action and may support a corrected filtered argument. Page 31 actually uses the false identification to pass from web calculations to a knot spectral sequence; a separately cited result may offer another route but does not validate this identification.
independent_verification.repair_check: Provide the appropriate iterated/associated-graded identification with a compatible filtration and naturality proof. No counterexample to the ultimate DGR inequality or the separately cited theorem is claimed.

problems.title: Planar Kauffman-state basis fails under the permitted t=1 specialization

source_claim.claim: For arbitrary coefficient ring with invertible t, quotienting planar singular-knot homology by coefficient torsion gives a finite Kauffman-state basis.

assumptions: Connected planar singular D2, no real crossings, outer thin marking
Torsion read charitably with NONZERO annihilator, not exploiting printed omission

counterexample.calculation: H0=Q[a,b,c,d]/(a,b-d,ab-cd,a-c,a+b-c-d)=Q[b]. Here a is marked outgoing variable; exchanging a,c is equivalent.
counterexample.complete_boundary_list: Singular deviation, inner trace deviation, unique inner coherent cycle avoiding mark, and linear L_S factor. Degree formula excludes other sources into unique degree0 generator.
counterexample.all_nonlocal_relations: Assign outer closed colored strand0, inner strandb, thick multiset{0,b}. Every adapted closed curve has equal colorwise incoming/outgoing counts; q=1 makes all nonlocal relations zero. Thus no hidden polynomial relation in b.
counterexample.contradiction: Q-torsion0 and infinite dimension versus finitely many Kauffman states.

counterevidence: Generic completed concentration may remain valid.
No counterexample to actual Z((q)) Theorem5.11 supplied.
problems.impact: Substantive coefficient-range error in a planar computation used for cube concentration.

correction.statement: Restrict to appropriate completed/localized coefficients and prove concentration there; justify t-small versus q-small completion direction. Arbitrary nonflat specialization is unavailable.
correction.verification_status: Supported within the explicitly stated boundary; see current English report and analytic notes

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The stated coefficient range permits k=Q,t=1. For the pointed planar single-dumbbell closure, the degree-zero boundary relations are a=0, b-d=0, ab-cd=0, a-c=0, a+b-c-d=0. Their quotient is Q[b]. Every nonlocal relation is also respected by assigning 0 to the outer strand and b to the inner strand, because closed-strand counts agree and t=1. Over Q no nonzero scalar torsion removes this infinite-dimensional degree-zero space, whereas the diagram has finitely many Kauffman states.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The claim's reduction through arbitrary specializations is nonflat and cannot be assumed valid. The witness lies inside the printed coefficient range but does not refute the generic completed calculation. The t^(1/2)-positive completion on p.43 and the q-positive completion with t=q^-2 in Theorem 5.11 require a compatible comparison; that additional issue remains a proof obligation, not another proved counterexample.
independent_verification.repair_check: Specify a completion/localization with the needed units and prove concentration there, together with the coefficient-change or completion-direction argument. The actual use for the Floer-cube vertices makes the unrestricted proposition failure Major.

problems.title: Abstract spectral-sequence isomorphism loses extension data

source_claim.claim: An isomorphism on one page induces an isomorphism of completed filtered abutments without a compatible filtered map.

assumptions: Actual pagewise identity of constant spectral sequences

counterexample.proof: Each associated graded is Z/2 in filtration0,1 and every differential0. Completions unchanged. Only M contains order4 element, so no group isomorphism. Any M->N kills F1 and cannot lift the required graded isomorphism.

counterevidence: The preceding source paragraph assumes an actual filtered map; an appropriately formulated comparison theorem is valid.
The particular free graded pieces may support a separate lifting proof; no such proof/map is supplied in the invoked argument on pp42-43.
The finite PID Bockstein argument does not use this false uniqueness principle.
problems.impact: TheoremA.2 is false under its printed hypotheses. Source p43 explicitly invokes spectral-sequence uniqueness, referring to AppendixA.1, to obtain the completed Kauffman-state conclusion of Proposition4.21 used in Section5/Theorem5.11. Neither a compatible filtered comparison map nor a particular lifting argument is supplied. Major for this core proof step, without disproving the completed conclusion or DGR inequality.

correction.statement: Require a compatible filtered chain/abutment map and verify graded comparison and convergence, or provide a separate lifting argument for these particular completed modules.
correction.verification_status: The complete finite-extension example and direct source dependency on pp42-43,55-56 were independently checked. The missing map/lifting is a required repair.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: Take degree-zero complexes M=Z/4 with F0=M,F1=2M,F2=0 and N=(Z/2)^2 with F0=N,F1 one summand,F2=0, extended exhaustively below. Both filtrations are complete and Hausdorff. Their constant spectral sequences have identical associated-graded Z/2 pieces, but their completed groups are not isomorphic: only M has an element of order four. Thus an abstract pagewise isomorphism cannot determine the filtered abutment without a compatible comparison map.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The preceding source paragraph correctly includes an actual filtered map. Page 43 explicitly invokes uniqueness of the spectral-sequence limit, referring to Appendix A.1, to obtain the completed free Kauffman-state/concentration conclusion in Proposition 4.21, then used in Section 5 including Theorem 5.11. Neither the general theorem nor that argument supplies the needed filtered comparison/lifts. Free graded pieces might permit an additional lifting proof, but that is not the printed proof.
independent_verification.repair_check: Retain and verify a filtered chain/abutment map or construct a separate lifting argument with convergence. The finite-extension witness refutes the general comparison theorem; it is not a counterexample to the particular completed Theorem 5.11 or DGR inequality. The actual core use warrants Major despite possible repair.

problems.title: Zero Bockstein page does not mean zero exact couple

source_claim.claim: The (k+1)-st exact couple vanishes even with a nonunit factor coprime to q-1.

counterexample.proof: H=L/((q-1)(q+1)); d1 on E1=Q⊕Q is multiplication2, hence E2=0. But D2=(q-1)H=L/(q+1)≠0, on which q-1 acts by−2 invertibly.
counterexample.typed_formula_correction: On p57, g∘h:B->B is the differential; printed g∘f has domainA, notB.

counterevidence: The final E∞ formula and finite stabilization remain true.
Pure-primary ExampleA.5 really has zero terminal exact couple.
problems.impact: Local exact-couple statement and typed formula need correction; main finite PID limit survives.

correction.statement: State that the E term vanishes and retain coprime torsion on D, or split it first; replace g∘f by g∘h.
correction.verification_status: Supported within the explicitly stated boundary; see current English report and analytic notes

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: For L=Q[q,q^-1] and the two-term free complex with differential (q-1)(q+1), the first Bockstein differential is multiplication by 2, so E2=0. The derived D term remains L/(q+1), nonzero, with q-1 acting by -2. A zero spectral-sequence page does not imply a zero exact couple. The source's printed g composed with f also has the wrong domain for the differential; g composed with h is required.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Only the E term needs to vanish for the conclusion. Splitting coprime torsion or using Smith normal form proves the finite stabilization/free-rank statement without the false zero-couple assertion.
independent_verification.repair_check: Replace the assertion by vanishing of E and correct the composition. Proposition A.7 itself is not disproved.
